Meeting header:

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for making time, um this is Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. we'll do a quick agenda, then hand off to Priya for the onboarding plan and Samir for technical details.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: hi Alex, thanks, yeah excited to get this moving. we have a pretty tight schedule, end of Q4 we'd like initial pilot in prod-ish, so hoping we can align today.
[00:30] Priya Nair: perfect, quick note - i'll be owning the playbook and the sprint runway. goal today: confirm success criteria, access, security blockers, and what we need to ship the pilot.
[00:42] Ravi Sharma: just to set context, our main constraint is that we need data isolation for training/customer data, and we have a hybrid infra - some workloads in our VPC, some in private racks.
[00:53] Samir Gupta: got it. from an SE perspective we're going to propose two tracks: 1) hosted Redwood API for quick ramp (sandbox) and 2) Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) for production isolation. switch to private when ready.
[01:10] Greta Holm: quick security note, we are SOC2 in progress and need KMS-based key management and audit logs for every inference call stored for 90 days. also want SSO SAML and RBAC.
[01:25] Alex Chen: that's totally understandable, we'll call that out in the runbook. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and audit log retention options; we'll share the SOC2 pack and the integration doc.
[01:36] Tomás Vega: are there network peering requirements for the VPC option? our infra team is strict about allowed inbound rules.
[01:45] Samir Gupta: yes, we'll provide a minimal set of required CIDR ranges and private endpoints. for the private deployment we can do an initial air-gapped package or VPC peering, depending on your security team's preference.
[01:58] Alex Chen: timeline question — you mentioned end of Q4 for a pilot in a production-like environment. is that firm?
[02:06] Lena Ortiz: it's an internal goal, not customer-facing yet, but we have exec deadlines. if the pilot can show 99th percentile latencies under 300ms for short prompts and cost estimates we can push forward.
[02:20] Priya Nair: noted. can you share expected traffic shape? average QPS and peak?
[02:27] Ravi Sharma: for the pilot it's low QPS, about 2-5 qps, bursty during demo, but production plans could be 50-100 qps eventually.
[02:36] Samir Gupta: great - that helps model batching and instance sizing. for 50-100 qps we'll likely recommend a Dedicated pool or private with multiple GPUs and batching configs.
[02:48] Speaker 3: (mumbles) also depends on the model size, if you're using a LLM with big context it changes things.
[02:55] Alex Chen: yeah good point, we should pick a model family early. Lena, do you have a preference for open models vs vendor proprietary?
[03:03] Lena Ortiz: prefer open models for cost and evaluation parity, but we may test a couple of closed models too for specific tasks.
[03:11] Priya Nair: action: we'll include a model recommendation appendix in the playbook with quantization and cost tradeoffs.
[03:20] Ravi Sharma: security question: how are keys rotated and how does audit logging handle PII? we want to make sure there's no tokens stored in clear.
[03:29] Samir Gupta: Redwood Private supports KMS integration and keys never leave your HSM; logs can be redacted or routed to your SIEM. we'll document the redaction knobs and retention controls.
[03:40] Greta Holm: also need code-level change logs and a simple runbook for incident response, like who to call if inference latency spikes.
[03:48] Priya Nair: we'll add an oncall + escalation appendix to the runbook with SLOs and playbooks.
[03:55] Alex Chen: i wanted to flag one tradeoff — if you go hosted initially you get faster time-to-value but less isolation; private is more work up front but cleaner for compliance. what matters more to you for the pilot?
[04:08] Lena Ortiz: for the pilot we can do hosted under a data-contract with redaction, but for go-live it has to be private. so hybrid approach preferred.
[04:18] Alex Chen: that aligns with what Samir said. we'll plan pilot on hosted sandbox then a short private proof-of-run.
[04:26] Samir Gupta: technical ask: we'll need a sample of your prompt patterns and two eval sets: one user-facing conversational set and one LLM-assisted control prompts. can you send 20-30 examples?
[04:38] Ravi Sharma: yes we can. Ravi will own prompts.
[04:42] Tomás Vega: what about observability? we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency.
[04:50] Samir Gupta: Redwood Console has per-route dashboards and token telemetry; we'll show a demo of the Console in the next technical deep dive.
[04:59] Speaker 2: (overlap) there's also an optimize tool that suggests batching and quantization.
[05:04] Priya Nair: right, Redwood Optimize can suggest batching levels and quant profiles by workload. we'll include optimization quickwins in the playbook.
[05:12] Lena Ortiz: will you help run a small quality regression check so we don't regress when switching quantization?
[05:18] Samir Gupta: yes, we recommend an eval harness — we'll run a quick baseline before and after.
[05:23] Alex Chen: ok, security doc sharing — Priya and I will drop links to the SOC2 summary, encryption integration guide, and our onboarding checklist right after this call. you'll see them in the follow-up email. (link note: onboarding playbook: https://redwood.example/playbooks/keystone-onboarding ; security pack: https://redwood.example/security/keystone-soc2)
[05:45] Greta Holm: thanks. also can you confirm SLA targets for dedicated pools? our procurement needs numbers for the contract.
[05:52] Alex Chen: Dedicated pools have committed throughput SLAs and latency windows; i'll include the SLA pdf and a draft term sheet in the follow-up.
[05:59] Ravi Sharma: procurement will also want references — can you share two enterprise references with similar compliance needs?
[06:06] Alex Chen: yes, we'll anonymize and share two references that have used private deployments.
[06:14] Lena Ortiz: great, last question on rollouts — how do you handle model rollbacks if an eval fails after a canary?
[06:22] Samir Gupta: Redwood Console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies to a pinned model version. we'll include a runbook example for a canary and rollback.
[06:33] Priya Nair: recap of immediate next steps: alex will share playbook + security docs; samir to prepare perf test plan; r avi/greta to share prompts and compliance artifacts; schedule technical deep dive for Console demo and perf run tentatively 2026-10-12.
[06:47] Tomás Vega: noted, i'll coordinate on the VPC peering window and share firewall contacts.
[06:53] Alex Chen: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the runbook. look forward to getting the pilot running.
[07:00] Lena Ortiz: thanks all.
